newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore plans billion dollar airport terminal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore plans billion dollar airport terminal.

text.p: Singapore, aiming to maintain its position as a leading air traffic hub, will build a third terminal at Changi airport at a cost of about Singapore $1.5 billion (U.S.$1.07 billion), officials said on Monday.

Fong Kok Wai, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) director of engineering, told a news conference the new terminal and related facilities would increase passenger handling capacity by about 20 million people a year.
Fong said the project would be funded by existing CAAS financial reserves and push Changi's annual passenger capacity to 64 million once the terminal opens in 2004.
The news conference followed a speech at Changi by Mah Bow Tan, Singapore's Minister for Communications, who made the official announcement that Terminal Three would go ahead.
Mah said the government decided to build the third terminal "to maintain Changi's position as a premier hub airport" before the two existing terminals reach full capacity, expected within 10 years.
Meanwhile, new airports likely to compete with Changi for passengers are due to become operational in 1998 at Sepang, Malaysia, and Chek Lap Kok, Hong Kong.
CAAS officials declined to say whether official estimates had been compiled on how much traffic Changi might lose to these airports after they come on stream.

Construction of a third Changi terminal, capable of handling next generation 600-seater super-jumbo aircraft, would benefit other Asian airports as the volume of international and intra-Asian travellers expands into the next century, Mah said.
"Without this development, prospects for other airports in the region would be much poorer," he told reporters.
"Detailed design will begin next year, and construction will begin when the design is ready, which we expect to be in 1999, with completion scheduled for 2003," Mah said.
Mah said Changi handled 23 million passengers in 1995 and 25 million were expected this year.
CAAS has forecast that Changi's two existing terminals would be handling 41 million passengers by 2006, almost their total combined capacity.
CAAS said Terminal Three would add 25 new aerobridge gates and the airport's "Skytrain" passenger transport system would be extended to link all three terminals.

Terminal Three would be built on a piece of open land opposite Terminal Two. Between the two is the proposed site of a new station linking Changi to Singapore's Mass Rapid Transit rail network, said CAAS officials.
